A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe BREX and ExIde. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices, including image-based prompts, support reliable comparison despite reflow and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of 13 LLMs on BREX, complexity analyses, human text-quality ratings, and annotation-agreement results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds a supervised fine-tuning comparison in Section 5.5 and Table 5.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 introduces the name Listwise Contextual Reasoning, but the unchanged Figure 15 already supplies business text and a list of rule pairs in v3. The extraction prompts and two-stage pipeline remain unchanged; the rewritten description does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same BREX documents, domains, and rule-extraction, operator-classification, and dependency-identification tasks. The new fine-tuning experiment changes the data split within this coverage, without adding a dataset or task scenario.

E2.justification: Section 5.5 and Table 5 add a LoRA-fine-tuned Qwen-30B-Instruct comparator against ExIde across the three tasks. This is a limited addition involving one base model; the original 13-model and five-prompt comparisons remain intact.

E3.justification: The added fine-tuning comparison uses 300 BREX samples for training and 109 for testing. This introduces a separate training and evaluation protocol, rather than revising the settings of the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 adds qualitative error analysis of the fine-tuned model's omitted or truncated rule-pair judgments, termed Rule Pair Dropping. The existing complexity analyses and all three Appendix A.7 case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 4's error bars and the ICC and Fleiss' Kappa reporting are unchanged. The new fine-tuning table provides point scores without introducing run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: On the new split, Table 5 adds ExIde/SFT scores of 83.90/84.70 for rule extraction, 63.60/72.40 for operator classification, and 40.84/24.16 for dependency identification. These are additional results under the new protocol; Tables 2–4 and the existing appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The rule schema, dependency definitions, and mathematical framework are retained. Section 4.2's explicit O(N^2) notation restates the quadratic growth already discussed in v3's limitations; no new proof or substantive formal reasoning is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same BREX and ExIde contributions and claims about executable grounding and reasoning-optimized models. The fine-tuning comparison adds supporting findings without changing these headline claims.

C2.justification: v4 attributes the fine-tuned model's dependency deficit to incomplete outputs and possible overfitting to training-output length or format. Section 4.2 also adds arguments about joint context reducing contradictory edges and inference overhead. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 documents LoRA, the Qwen-30B-Instruct base model, and the sample allocation for the new comparison. It does not supply the training hyperparameters or decoding limits. Existing appendix prompts and code/data access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Hu et al. (2022) for LoRA and extends its empirical positioning against supervised fine-tuning. Section 2 and Appendix A.4 otherwise retain the same cited works and distinctions between action-centric and rule-centric research.

P1.justification: Changes comprise a localized Section 4.2 rewrite, new Section 5.5 and acknowledgements, updated affiliations, and numbered limitations and ethics sections. Most prose is retained. The final dependency-complexity paragraph in Section 5.4 is duplicated in v4.

P2.justification: v4 adds the fine-tuning Table 5 and renumbers the former appendix Tables 5–10 as Tables 6–11. Existing displays are repositioned, including grouping Figures 5–7 on one page. Plot content and appendix prompt images remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies v3's ambiguous dependency-inference description by aligning Section 4.2 with Figure 15, while Table 5 tests the motivation for prompting rather than fine-tuning. These provide a modest gain in clarity and evidence. Sparse training and decoding details limit the new causal interpretation, and Section 5.4 introduces paragraph duplication.
